newsitem.title: FRANCE: S&P says French banks remain Europe's laggards.
newsitem.headline: S&P says French banks remain Europe's laggards.

text.p: French banks remain among the least profitable in continental Europe and with margins low and declining, 1997 should be a year of further restructuring, rating agency Standard & Poors ADEF said on Monday.

"The French banking system remains, along with the Italian system, one of the least profitable in continental Europe, not to mention the United States and the United Kingdom," S&P said in a report published on Monday.
In the report S&P ADEF said the improvements seen in net banking income at the main French banks in 1996 were largely due to their good performance in financial markets, by nature a volatile sector.

The report said, however, the credit quality of the main French banking groups had not deteriorated as much in 1996 as it had in previous years and half of the downgrades affected small institutions generally specialising in property.
Robert Scott Bugie, director, financial institutions at S&P ADEF, said at a news conference there would probaby be fewer reductions in French bank ratings this year and more increases than in 1996.

But he said any upgrades in 1997 would probably be due to takeovers or mergers of institutions by banks with better ratings, the reason for the upgrades in 1996, rather than significant intrinsic improvements at the banks concerned.
In 1996, 14 French bank ratings were downgraded or put on creditwatch with negative implications by S&P, while six were upgraded or put on creditwatch with positive implications.
The report also said French banks would need to make significant investments in technical systems to prepare for the planned introduction of a single European currency in 1999.

It said between 15 and 25 billion francs was generally regarded as the total amount the sector would need to spend during the next three to four years, although that figure did not take account of any reduction in revenue from foreign exchange and international transfers.

Bugie said French banks appeared to be preoccupied by problems in the domestic market due to low profitability and did not have the means to invest in readiness for increased competition from other European banks.
"French banks appear rather on the defensive as regards international competition, while their Swiss, German, Dutch and even Spanish competitors are developing ambitious strategies," the report said.
